ApiReply.description:
What a route that sends the engine a command answers over HTTP.

Done: `200` with `{"status": "ok"}`, and `uuid` when the command made
something, `data` when it reports something. Refused by the engine: `400`,
`404`, `500` or `503` with `{"error": "invalid_input" | "not_found" |
"internal" | "unavailable", "message": "…"}`. A request that cannot be read
(bad JSON, a missing field, no JSON content type) gets a plain-text `400`,
`415` or `422` instead, and a few routes answer some failures in plain text.

How content is mapped onto a surface.

The deck's texture is simply smaller: everything downstream samples it
across the full frame, so it is scaled up where it is used.

is_circular.description: Whether the contour approximates a circle.

oneOf.description:
Editable curve outline captured during SVG import (control points
preserved). `None` for raster/DXF detection, which produce polylines only.

DetectionMethod.description: Method used to produce the binary image for contour detection.

DetectionParams.description: Parameters controlling the contour detection pipeline.

blur_radius.description: Gaussian blur radius applied before edge detection.

oneOf.description: Detection method: Canny or Threshold.
Post-processing hull mode.

threshold.description: Threshold value for binary image creation (0-255).

DisplayLinkSnapshot.description:
The display link that starts frames: its callbacks, the frames they
asked for, and the redraws the frame loop saw.

collapsed.description:
Asks that reached the frame loop while the one before was still
waiting to be drawn: merged into one frame, a refresh with none.

link_events.description: Of those asks, the ones that reached the frame loop.

recent.description: The last callbacks (about five seconds' worth), oldest first.

skipped_redraws.description: Of those, the ones not drawn (with `clock_timestamps` on).

unrequested_redraws.description:
Redraws macOS asked for by itself (a window needing display), not
the frame loop.

DomemasterResolution.description:
Domemaster resolution presets.

Square by definition: a domemaster is a circular fisheye image inscribed in a
square, so it is sized by the dome's projectors rather than by the master
render resolution it samples from.

resolution.description:
Domemaster output size. Square, so it is a preset rather than a width
and height: `R1K` (1024²), `R2K` (2048²), or `R4K` (4096²).

source.description: The object to copy beside itself. The clipboard is left alone.

unit.description: Unit of the duration (seconds or beats).

EdgeBlendConfig.description: Edge blending configuration for an output — four independent edges.

gamma.description: Gamma curve exponent for the blend ramp (typically 1.0–3.0).

width.description: Blend zone width as fraction of output dimension (0.0–0.5).

EdgeBlendMode.description: Controls whether edge blend config is user-set or auto-computed from surface topology.

EffectMask.description: A mask: where, how soft its edge, and which side of it the effect is on.

feather.description:
How soft the edge is: the width of the fade across it, in pixels of a
1080-line picture (whatever the size), half inside the shape and half
outside. 0 is a clean edge.

invert.description: The effect outside the shape, and the picture as it was inside.

oneOf.description: A deck's pre-composite chain, by deck UUID.

Deck.description: A deck's pre-composite chain, by deck UUID.

oneOf.description: A channel's post-composite chain, by channel UUID.

Channel.description: A channel's post-composite chain, by channel UUID.

oneOf.description: The master output chain.

EffectTarget.description:
Identifies which effect chain to operate on.

Used for chain-scoped operations (append an effect, reorder within a chain).
Operations on an *existing* effect address it by its own UUID instead — see
[`/spec/api-addressing.md`].

FramePart.description: Time a frame spent on one part.

freq_high.description: Upper bound of the frequency range in Hz.

freq_low.description: Lower bound of the frequency range in Hz.

GlobalAction.description:
A global app action a Trigger button can fire. These require app-layer
context and reuse the same dispatch (and pending-flag drain) as the MIDI
`action/*` paths — see `app/inputs.rs`.

expect.description:
The step this press is meant for, by UUID: refused if another is
next by now, so a press never lands on the step after the one meant.

fade.description: Dissolve rather than cut. On unless said otherwise.

target.description: Index of the step to jump to.

ms_per_s.description:
Milliseconds of GPU time per second: its share of the time the GPU
was busy with Nida's work, a moment shared equally among the runs
going on then — the parts add up to `busy_pct` (×10).

runs_per_s.description: How many times it ran per second.

GpuTimeSnapshot.description: Where Nida's GPU time went over the last second.

busy_pct.description:
The share of the second Nida's work was running on the GPU (0–100),
command buffers that overlapped counted once. The whole GPU's
`gpu_busy_pct` adds other apps' work and the screens' compositing.

groups.description:
GPU time by part of the app — the show, the control window, its
previews, the outputs, wgpu's own uploads — most first.

parts.description: GPU time by command buffer label, most first.

HtmlInteractiveBody.description: Body for opening/closing the interactive window of an HTML deck.

open.description: True to open the interactive window, false to close it.

url.description: HTML content URL or local file path.

HullMode.description: Post-processing hull mode applied after simplification.

oneOf.description: Performance mode holds; the arrangement stays inert.
A designated deck is shown until the transport reaches the arranged range.

ShowDeck.description: A designated deck is shown until the transport reaches the arranged range.

IdleBehaviour.description:
What renders while the arrangement is not driving anything.

"Run this loop until the schedule starts" is a normal installation
requirement, so the pre-show state needs something to *be* rather than
something to fail at. See /spec/transport.md § Idle behaviour.

idle.description: What renders outside the arranged range.

InputAudio.description:
A new input's own sound: a sound device, or two of its channels, heard
as the input goes on air — a camera or capture card's sound, vMix's
"Audio" when adding a camera.

left.description: Device channel for the left side (0-based).

right.description: Device channel for the right side; the same as `left` for mono.

InputPacing.description: A live input's frames on their way into the show.

behind_ms.description:
How long before its show frame was due on screen the frame shown was
captured, milliseconds: the input's delay inside Nida, past the
camera's own (see `frame_picker`). The outputs' own delay to their
glass comes on top.

oneOf.description:
A camera or capture card, by id from `GET /api/library/cameras`, at
one of its formats (`GET /api/state/cameras`) or its best.
An NDI source on the network, by its full name.
A display or window.
A solid colour, straight RGBA 0 to 1.
A web page.

A generator from the shader library (`GET /api/library/generators`),
by name.

Another input's picture, by its channel's UUID: as a layer, that input
inside this one; as a new input, a copy of it that can be sized and
placed on its own (vMix's virtual input). Drawn once for both.

Clips, sound files and pictures played one after another, as vMix's
List input.

A count down, count to a time, count up or the time of day, drawn
as text over clear.

A PowerPoint deck, played by PowerPoint on this computer in a window
Nida captures — its transitions, animations and videos as PowerPoint
plays them — and moved on from Nida (macOS).

A presenter view of a PowerPoint input, for the speaker's screen: its
slide, live, with the speaker notes, what comes next and the talk's
clocks. `deck_uuid` is the PowerPoint input's layer.

InputSource.description:
What a new input shows, for [`EngineCommand::AddInput`]: a live source,
as vMix's Add Input window offers them. Files come in through the file
dialog instead, a new input each.

after_vert_idx.description: Index of the existing vertex after which to insert.

position.description: Position of the new vertex as [x, y].

LayerMaskBody.description: A layer's own mask, or `null` to take it away.

oneOf.description:
Its part of the source's picture: this rectangle, in the picture's
pixels. Screens taking parts of one source continue one image.
The whole picture, as large as fits; the rest of the screen is black.
The screen covered, the picture's overflow cut off.
The whole picture pulled to the screen's shape.

LedFit.description: How a screen shows its source.

LedLayout.description: The screens one output's feed carries.

feed.description:
The feed's size in pixels: what the LED processor takes in, such as
1920×1080 or 3840×2160.

screens.description: The screens, drawn in order (a later one covers an earlier one).

test_card.description:
Every screen shows a test card — its name, size, border and a grid —
instead of its picture, to line the feed up with the processor.

LedScreen.description: One LED screen: where it sits in the feed and what it shows.

at.description: Its top-left corner in the feed, in pixels.

fit.description: How the picture is put on it.

size.description: The screen's size in LED pixels, as the LED technician gives it.

source.description: What it shows: `Master` (Main) or a bus's program.

uuid.description: Stable id (8-char hex); given on the way in when left empty.

LevelerConfig.description:
A source's leveler: brings each speaker slowly to the same loudness, as a
radio station's processor does, so a soft speaker after a loud one needs no
hand on the fader. It holds still through pauses, so it never pumps the
room's noise up between sentences.

hold_below_db.description:
Below this average level, dBFS (−80 to −20), it takes the sound for a
pause or the room and holds still.

max_boost_db.description: The most it turns a soft voice up, 0–24 dB.

max_cut_db.description: The most it turns a loud voice down, 0–24 dB.

speed_secs.description:
How slowly it moves, 0.5–20 s: about the time it takes to make up most
of a difference. It turns down three times as fast as it turns up.

target_db.description:
The level it rides the voice to: the average (RMS) level, dBFS,
−40 to −6.

LimiterConfig.description:
A bus's limiter: the last thing before its recordings, streams and
screens, so a shout, a dropped microphone or a loud clip can never clip
them. It looks a little ahead to turn down before a peak arrives.

ceiling_db.description: The highest a sample may go, dBFS, −12 to 0.

release_ms.description: How quickly it lets go after a peak, 10–1000 ms.

at_ms.description: When it came, in milliseconds after the link started.

shown_ms.description:
The refresh it is for — the time macOS stamped it with — in the same
milliseconds; none when macOS gave none.

oneOf.description: Range internal playback wraps within. `null` clears the loop.

LoopRegion.description: A range of show positions, in seconds, that internal playback wraps within.

LowCutConfig.description: A source's low cut: the rumble, handling noise and hum under a voice.

hz.description: Where it starts to cut, 20–400 Hz. Speech has little below 100 Hz.

slope_db.description: How steeply below it: 12 or 24 dB an octave.

LtcInput.description:
Which audio input carries LTC.

Held beside the preference rather than inside it: this is a patch decision
that should survive switching to `Auto` and back, and burying it in one
enum variant would lose it on every switch.
See /spec/timecode.md § Preference and Priority.

channel.description: Zero-based channel index within that device.

oneOf.description:
Rate to read the signal at, or `None` to infer it from cadence.

Only 29.97 non-drop actually needs naming: it is a thousandth away from
30 in the signal and identical in the labels, but 3.6 seconds an hour
apart in position. See [`ltc::LtcDecoder::set_rate_override`].

Audio input carrying LTC, and the channel of it. `null` stops listening,
which also releases the device.
Ease-in (slow start): `v²`.
Ease-out (fast start): `sqrt(v)`.
Ease-in-out (smoothstep): `v²(3 - 2v)`.
Quantize into `n` discrete levels (n≥2).

MacroCurve.description:
Response curve applied to a macro's 0..1 value before it is mapped to a
target's `[min, max]` sub-range. All curves are pure `[0,1] -> [0,1]`.

amount.description: Modulation depth (0.0–1.0), added as an offset to the macro's manual set point.

source_id.description: UUID of the modulation source (LFO/ADSR/etc.) that drives this macro's value.

oneOf.description: Nothing: black.
A channel, every deck in it layered, by channel UUID.

Channel.description: A channel, every deck in it layered, by channel UUID.

oneOf.description: One deck on its own, by deck UUID.

Deck.description: One deck on its own, by deck UUID.

MainTransition.description: How a take that is not a cut changes Main — vMix's transitions.

oneOf.description: A rectangle, by its left, top, width and height.

The ellipse inside that rectangle — a circle, when it is square on
the screen.
An outline drawn by hand, closed back to its first point.

device_id.description: Numeric identifier of the MIDI device.

enabled.description: Whether the device should be enabled.

oneOf.description: CC message: (`device_id`, channel, `cc_number`)
Note message: (`device_id`, channel, `note_number`)

MidiKey.description:
Unique identifier for a MIDI control (for mapping).
Includes `device_id` so the same CC# on different devices maps independently.

mode.description:
`program`: one channel or input on Main with overlays on top;
`layered`: every channel at its fader.

oneOf.description: Audio source device ID, or null for the default source.

before_deck_uuid.description: Put it just before this deck in that channel; omit for the end.

dst_channel_uuid.description: UUID of the channel to move the deck into (its own channel reorders).

anchor_idx.description: Index of the curve-path anchor to move.

pos.description: New anchor position [x, y] in normalised coordinates.

handle.description: Which control handle of the cubic segment (C1 or C2).

pos.description: New handle position [x, y] in normalised coordinates.

segment_idx.description: Index of the cubic segment whose control handle is being moved.

position.description: New [x, y] position in normalised coordinates.

horizontal.description:
`true` = a horizontal edge ((r,c)→(r,c+1)); `false` = a vertical edge
((r,c)→(r+1,c)).

position.description: New [x, y] position in normalised coordinates.

which.description: Which handle of the edge: 0 (near start anchor) or 1 (near end anchor).

source_name.description: Name of the NDI source to receive.

OnScreenStats.description:
How evenly a window's frames reached the screen since it opened, from
the system's own report of when each was shown (macOS; zeros elsewhere).

early.description: Frames replaced less than half a frame after they came up.

expected_ms.description: How long each frame should stay up, ms.

hitches.description:
Frames up more than half a frame too long: the one before repeated,
the hitch an eye sees in a moving slide.

interval_mean_ms.description: Mean and spread of the last 300 times between frames coming up, ms.

OutputAudioBusBody.description: The audio bus an output carries.

OutputPacing.description: One output window's presents, counted since it opened.

follows_clock.description: On the screen whose refresh starts frames: every frame presented.

on_screen.description: How evenly its frames reached the screen.

pace_skipped.description: Frames drawn but not presented, to keep to the display's rate.

unavailable.description: Frames the window had nowhere to present.

oneOf.description: The master mix (final composited output)
A specific channel's composited output (by index)

Channel.description: A specific channel's composited output (by index)

oneOf.description:
A subset of channels composited together (sub-mix).
Each channel contributes with its own opacity and blend mode.
Master effects are NOT applied to sub-mixes.

Channels.description:
A subset of channels composited together (sub-mix).
Each channel contributes with its own opacity and blend mode.
Master effects are NOT applied to sub-mixes.

oneOf.description: A specific deck's raw output (channel index, deck index)

items.description: A specific deck's raw output (channel index, deck index)

Deck.description: A specific deck's raw output (channel index, deck index)

oneOf.description: The domemaster fisheye output (equidistant azimuthal projection)

A production bus's Program, by stable bus UUID.

The destination follows whatever that bus has on air, so a `CUT` on the
bus changes this output and nothing else. Resolved once per frame
against the bus's *effective* program — a route the bus cannot resolve,
or one held black by a partial load, reads black here rather than
falling back to some other source.

BusProgram.description:
A production bus's Program, by stable bus UUID.

The destination follows whatever that bus has on air, so a `CUT` on the
bus changes this output and nothing else. Resolved once per frame
against the bus's *effective* program — a route the bus cannot resolve,
or one held black by a partial load, reads black here rather than
falling back to some other source.

OutputSource.description: Content source that an output window can display

oneOf.description: Floating window (default)
Fullscreen/borderless on a specific monitor (identified by name + index)

Display.description: Fullscreen/borderless on a specific monitor (identified by name + index)

monitor_index.description: Index into the available monitors list (for lookup)

oneOf.description: Record frames to a video file via ffmpeg subprocess

Recording.description: Record frames to a video file via ffmpeg subprocess

audio_device.description: Audio passthrough device NAME (None = silent). See spec/audio-passthrough.md.

oneOf.description: Stream frames via SRT (Secure Reliable Transport) through ffmpeg

SrtStream.description: Stream frames via SRT (Secure Reliable Transport) through ffmpeg

oneOf.description: Stream frames as HLS segments via ffmpeg

HlsStream.description: Stream frames as HLS segments via ffmpeg

oneOf.description: Stream frames as DASH segments via ffmpeg

DashStream.description: Stream frames as DASH segments via ffmpeg

oneOf.description: Push frames to an RTMP/RTMPS ingest endpoint via ffmpeg

RtmpStream.description: Push frames to an RTMP/RTMPS ingest endpoint via ffmpeg

codec_contract.description: Receiver codec signaling contract. Legacy is the interoperable default.

oneOf.description: Send frames over NDI network protocol

NdiSend.description: Send frames over NDI network protocol

oneOf.description: Publish frames via Syphon (macOS inter-app sharing)

SyphonServer.description: Publish frames via Syphon (macOS inter-app sharing)

oneOf.description:
A Blackmagic DeckLink device's video out — an UltraStudio Monitor 3G:
HDMI and SDI — in its format named `mode` ("1080p60" …). See
`crate::decklink`.

DeckLink.description:
A Blackmagic DeckLink device's video out — an UltraStudio Monitor 3G:
HDMI and SDI — in its format named `mode` ("1080p60" …). See
`crate::decklink`.

full_range.description:
Full levels — black at 0, white at 255 (1 and 254: 0 and 255 are
the signal's own) — for a display set to take them; off, video
levels, black at 16 and white at 235, as video gear takes them.

oneOf.description:
The stream: one encode sent to up to four RTMP destinations. Its
settings live with the stream (`crate::streaming`), and it never
appears among the outputs — the STREAM button runs it.

The recording: the REC button's file. Like the stream, its settings
live with it (`crate::record`) and it is never among the outputs.

OutputTarget.description: Where an output sends its content — unified across windowed and headless outputs.

OverlayBody.description: Whether a channel is an overlay.

OverlayOnBody.description: An overlay switched on or off.

PacingSnapshot.description:
Per-frame engine state snapshot — plain data, no GPU types, no lifetimes.

Produced by `VardaApp` each frame. Distributed to consumers via watch channel.
`UIData` is derived from this for the egui UI consumer.
How evenly frames are started and shown — for telling a judder's cause:
frames started late (the renderer), or presented unevenly (an output).

clock.description:
What starts each frame: a screen's refresh ("display 2 at 60.00 Hz,
every refresh") or Nida's own timer ("timer at 60 fps").

clock_timestamps.description:
Frames asked for by the refresh each display-link callback is
stamped for, not by counting callbacks (see `SetClockTimestamps`).

control_on_screen.description: How evenly the control window's frames reached its screen.

control_parts.description:
Where the control window's frames' time goes, now that it draws on
the main thread apart from the engine: each part's mean and worst,
the costliest first — "ui" (laying it out), "engine wait" (for the
engine thread to finish a frame), "ui acquire" (for a frame of its
own to draw into), and so on.

control_queue.description: The control window's frames waiting to be shown.

control_slow_frames.description: The control window's last slow frames, part by part.

control_vsync.description:
The control window presents in step with its screen's refresh (see
`SetControlVsync`).

oneOf.description:
The display link's callbacks and what came of them, when a screen's
refresh starts frames. Updated every tenth frame.

frame_hold.description: Each frame held on screen for a frame's time (see `SetFrameHold`).

frame_pacing.description: What starts each frame (see the `SetFramePacing` command).

frames_in_flight.description:
Frames the GPU may still be drawing when the next starts (see the
`SetFramesInFlight` command).

gpu_busy_pct.description:
How busy the GPU is (0–100), as the OS reports it (macOS: the
accelerator's "Device Utilization %"); absent where it does not.

oneOf.description:
Where Nida's GPU time went over the last second, by part of the app
(macOS: when each command buffer ran on the GPU); absent elsewhere.

inputs.description: Each live camera's and captured screen's delay inside Nida.

interval_mean_ms.description:
Time between the starts of the last frames (about five seconds of
them), in milliseconds.

late_frames.description:
Of those, frames started more than half a frame late: a screen
showing every frame showed the one before twice.

outputs.description: Each output window's presents since it opened.

parts.description:
Where frames' time goes: each part's mean and worst over the last
frames, the costliest first — "ui", "gpu wait", "mixer", a window's
"acquire" (its wait for a frame to draw into) and "draw", "ui present",
and "start delay" (from the refresh that called for a frame to its
start).

slow_frames.description:
The last frames (up to 20) that were busy for most of a frame's time,
started half a frame after their refresh, or came half a frame late,
part by part.

ParamValue.description: Parameter value types matching ISF input types

PartStats.description: One part of the frame loop's time.

oneOf.description: This deck's channel, just after it in the stack: in front of it.

AfterDeck.description: This deck's channel, just after it in the stack: in front of it.

oneOf.description: The end of this channel.
This effect's chain, directly after it.

AfterEffect.description: This effect's chain, directly after it.

oneOf.description: The end of a deck, channel, or master chain.

IntoChain.description: The end of a deck, channel, or master chain.

oneOf.description: A new channel at the end of the mixer.

PasteTarget.description:
Where a paste lands.

The `After*` forms are what a right-click uses, so a copy arrives next to
the thing the menu was opened on — a deck's just after it in its
channel's stack, in front of it, which the lists of layers show above
it; the `Into*` forms append, which is what the container's own menu and
an API caller mean.

oneOf.description: Straight line to `to`.
Cubic bezier with control points `c1`, `c2`, ending at `to`.

Cubic.description: Cubic bezier with control points `c1`, `c2`, ending at `to`.

PathSegment.description:
One segment of a [`SurfacePath`]. Each segment ends at `to`; its start is the
previous segment's endpoint (or the path's `start` for the first segment).

pacing.description: How evenly frames are started and shown.

PlayAction.description: What a step does to something that runs: a clip, a playlist or a timer.

PlaylistItem.description: One thing in a playlist: a clip, a sound file or a picture, by its path.

preference.description:
`Auto` (LTC if patched and arriving, else MTC), `ForceLtc`,
`{"ForceMtc": {"device_id": 2}}`, or `Off`.

PresentationDepth.description: Requested and resolved SDR integer precision at an output boundary.

PresentationRequest.description: Persisted precision and dithering request for one output.

dither.description: Whether deterministic destination-aware dithering is enabled.

video_levels.description:
Whether the picture goes out in video levels — black at code 16 and
white at 235 (64 and 940 at ten bits) — for a screen that is video
gear and reads it so: a switcher's HDMI input, an LED processor. Off,
full levels, 0–255, as a monitor takes. Chosen per output; off by
default.

radius.description: New radius for the circle surface.

rate.description: Frame rate positions are displayed and quantised at.

RateMode.description:
How a stream's video bit rate is held. Measured at 1080p50 against the
rate set (see docs/17-streaming.md): the media engine's Constant pads a
talk's slides and camera bubbles to the rate with three quarters filler.

seconds.description: Ramp length back to the automated value. Omit for the default.

armed.description: Whether live control writes are kept as automation.

RecordCodec.description: The video codec of a recording.

RecordFormat.description: The file a recording is written as.

audio_bus.description:
The audio-mixer bus recorded; `None` is the first (Master). With no
bus at all the file carries silence, so it always has a sound track.

audio_kbps.description: AAC bit rate in kbit/s (`ProRes` files carry uncompressed sound).

fps.description: Frames per second; `None` is Varda's own.

source.description: The picture: the master, or a bus's Program.

video_kbps.description:
Video bit rate in kbit/s; `None` picks one for the size and frame
rate. Not used for `ProRes`.

RecordSnapshot.description: Recording as the API and state show it.

bytes.description: Bytes written to the current file so far.

dropped.description:
Frames the encoder could not take; each is covered by repeating the
one before.

files.description:
Every file of this take, in order — more than one if the encoder had
to start again.

fps.description: The rate frames reach the encoder at, as it was started.

free_bytes.description: Free space where the files go, in bytes.

last_file.description: The last finished recording, for "Show in Finder".

problem.description: What is wrong, when something is.

allOf.description: Visibility span in show seconds, with its fades.

RegionConfig.description:
A span during which a deck is visible.

Not a container for content: the deck exists in the scene whether or not any
region covers it, and a region only says *when*.

end.description: Transport position, in seconds, where the region ends.

fade_in.description: Fade-in duration in seconds, measured from `start`.

fade_out.description: Fade-out duration in seconds, measured back from `end`.

start.description: Transport position, in seconds, where the region begins.

key.description: MIDI key identifying the mapping to remove.

target_source_id.description: UUID of the modulation source being modulated.

name.description: New display name for the surface.

from_idx.description: Current position of the deck within its channel.

to_idx.description: Target position of the deck within its channel.

from_idx.description: Current index of the effect within the chain.

options.description: Options passed to the analyzer (optional, default empty object).

names.description: Parameters to reset; empty or left out resets them all.

`true`: the render resolution follows the largest screen an output is
on (a 4K TV gets a 4K picture). `false`: it stays at its current size.
Setting a resolution with `PUT /api/resolution` also turns Auto off.

angle.description: Rotation in radians (clockwise in canvas space, y-down).

pivot.description: Pivot point [x, y] in normalised coordinates.

Codec signaling contract declared by an RTMP/RTMPS endpoint.

URL scheme alone cannot establish Enhanced RTMP support, so this value is
explicit and persisted with the target.

RtmpMode.description: RTMP connection mode: pull from a remote server or listen for incoming pushes.

secs.description: Seconds the buses take to fade to a step. Finite and positive.

pivot.description: Pivot point [x, y] in normalised coordinates.

ScalingMode.description: Scaling mode for non-shader sources (images, video)

Capture target in handle-free form. Either `{"kind":"display","name":"..."}`
or `{"kind":"window","app":"...","title":"..."}` — matched against the last
enumeration, so call `POST /api/devices/screen/scan` first if unsure.

monitor_name.description: Name of the display monitor to target.

config.description: Edge blending configuration (four edges with enabled, width, gamma).

oneOf.description: The screens the feed carries; `null` makes it an ordinary output.

SetOutputSourceBody.description: Body for routing a headless output.

path.description:
Slash-separated path identifying the parameter, e.g.
`deck/<deck_uuid>/effect/<effect_uuid>/param/<name>`.

value.description:
New value: a plain number, `true`/`false`, four numbers for a colour
(RGBA) or two for a point. A number is a control position, as MIDI
and OSC send it, not the value itself — for a generator or effect
parameter 0 is its min and 1 its max, an integer one's choices split
evenly between; other paths scale it their own way.

shader_name.description: Shader name for the transition, or null to clear.

bound.description:
`true` = auto-conform the warp to the surface shape; `false` = unbind for
manual fine-tuning (materialises the conforming warp).

position.description: New [x, y] position for the corner in normalised coordinates.
New [x, y] position in normalised coordinates.

shader_name.description: Shader name, or null to clear.

sides.description: Number of polygon sides for the circle approximation.

SlowFrame.description: A frame that ran long or started late, part by part.

at_secs.description: When it started, in seconds after the first frame.

busy_ms.description: From its start to its end.

interval_ms.description: From the start of the frame before.

parts.description: Its parts over 0.3 ms, in the order spent.

start_delay_ms.description:
From the refresh that called for it to its start, when a screen's
refresh starts frames.

SrtMode.description: SRT connection mode — listener waits for connections, caller connects out.

channel_uuid.description: UUID of the channel the step references.

unit.description: Unit of the duration (seconds or beats).

StepMainBody.description: What a step takes to Main.

oneOf.description:
`{"Channel": "<uuid>"}`, `{"Deck": "<uuid>"}` or `"Black"` — or `null`
to leave Main as it is.

StepOverlayBody.description: Whether a step switches an overlay channel on or off.

on.description: `true` on, `false` off — or `null` to leave it as it is.

StepPlayBody.description: What a step does to a clip, a playlist or a timer.

oneOf.description:
`"start"` (from its beginning), `"resume"`, `"pause"` or `"stop"`
(back at its beginning) — or `null` for nothing.

StepScreenBody.description: What a bus shows in a step.

oneOf.description:
`"Black"`, `"Master"`, `{"Channel": "<uuid>"}` or `{"Deck": "<uuid>"}`
— or `null` to leave the bus as it is when the step is taken.

step_idx.description: Zero-based index of the step to update.

shader_name.description: Shader name for the transition, or null to clear.

StepThenBody.description: When a step goes on to the next by itself.

secs.description:
Seconds after the step is taken (more than none, an hour at most; no
sooner than the step's own fade is done) — or `null` to wait for GO.

steps.description: Step values for the sequencer (0.0–1.0 each).

key.description: Stream key; leave out to keep the one saved.

password.description: Leave out to keep the one saved.

StreamEncoder.description: Which H.264 encoder a stream uses.

mode.description: Stream connection mode (caller or listener for SRT).

StreamOptions.description:
What is streamed and how: shared by every destination, since the picture
is encoded once.

adaptive.description:
Lower the video bit rate while live when the upload cannot carry it,
and raise it again when it can, instead of losing parts of the stream
(see [`adaptive`]): on the media engine, encoded in Nida. Can be
switched while live there.

audio_bus.description:
The audio-mixer bus the stream carries, by UUID. `None` is the first
bus (Master); with no bus at all the stream carries silence, since
some platforms refuse a stream without sound.

audio_kbps.description: AAC audio bit rate in kbit/s.

buffer_secs.description:
Seconds of stream each destination can fall behind when its upload
slows, and catch up on afterwards, before any is lost. Bigger rides
out longer dips in venue internet; it cannot make up for an upload
that is too slow all the time.

fps.description: Frames per second sent; `None` is Varda's own frame rate.

keyframe_secs.description: Seconds between keyframes. Two is what most platforms ask for.

rate_mode.description: How the video bit rate is held (see [`RateMode`]).

source.description: The picture: the master, or a bus's Program.

video_kbps.description:
Video bit rate in kbit/s, constant. Changes while live for a stream
encoded in Nida (see [`StreamStatus::rate_live`]).

width.description: Picture size sent, scaled on the GPU from the source.

StreamSnapshot.description:
The stream as the API and state show it. Stream keys and passwords never
leave Varda: a key is shown by its last characters, a password only as
set or not.

oneOf.description:
The video bit rate following the upload, while it does; `None` while
it stays as set.

encoder_dropped.description:
Frames the encoder could not take since the stream started; each is
covered by repeating the one before.

encoder_dropped_secs.description:
The time those frames would have covered, in seconds: each counts its
own slot at the pace the show ran then.

encoder_fps.description:
The rate frames reach the encoder at, as it was started — 0 while
stopped.

encoder_problem.description:
Something wrong with the encoder itself: it stopped, or cannot keep
up with the frame rate.

rate_live.description:
The video bit rate, and whether it follows the upload, can be changed
while live: the stream is encoded in Nida.

oneOf.description:
How the running stream's rate is held, which may differ from the one
set (see [`RatePlan`]); `None` while stopped.

rate_note.description: Why it differs from the one set, or the encoder from the one chosen.

stream_fps.description: The rate the stream is sent at, as the encoder was started.

stream_kbps.description:
What the stream is at, sound and picture, in kbit/s, as the encoder
puts it out (see `Fanout::input_kbps`); `None` until measured.

SurfaceOutputType.description: How this surface connects to physical output hardware

SurfacePath.description: An editable curve outline for a surface, in normalized canvas coords [0..1].

closed.description:
Whether the outline is closed. Surfaces render closed regardless; this
records authoring intent for edit-time handles.

segments.description: Ordered segments; each continues from the previous endpoint.

start.description: Starting point of the path (first vertex of the flattened polygon).

SurfaceReorderOp.description:
A stacking-order move for a surface (8i.12). The `SurfaceManager.surfaces`
Vec order is authoritative (index 0 = bottom/drawn-first, last = top).

server_name.description: Name of the Syphon server to receive.

fade.description:
Take it with Main's transition (fade, merge, wipe, slide, zoom or
iris) over the fade time, rather than cut.

Dissolve — every bus over the rundown's fade time, Main by its own
fade — rather than cut.

TapSourceBody.description: Which Varda-internal output a tap deck reads. See spec/program-tap.md.

TimeFormat.description: How a length of time is written.

Timebase.description: Which notion of time a consumer follows.

timebase.description: Which notion of time the source follows.

oneOf.description: LTC if an input is named and it is arriving, otherwise MTC.

The named LTC input only. Legible as "no input selected" when there is
none, rather than silently following MIDI instead.

Ignore timecode entirely. Unlike the tempo clock, timecode has a
plausible "definitely not during this rehearsal" state.

TimecodePreference.description: Which signal the transport should follow.

TimecodeRate.description:
Frame rate used to display and quantise timecode positions.

Defined here rather than with the timecode receiver because the arrangement
ruler needs to render `HH:MM:SS:FF` before any timecode exists.
See /spec/arrangement.md § `TimecodeRate` ownership.

box_color.description:
The box behind the numbers — none at 0 opacity, which leaves the
background see-through.

caption.description: A line of text over the numbers ("Back in"), none when empty.

font.description:
A font family installed on the computer; one not found falls back
to the system's sans serif.

margin.description: Room kept from the frame's edges, as a share of its height.

outline_color.description:
An outline round the numbers, for reading them over a picture: its
width as a share of their height, none at 0.

over_color.description: The colour at zero, and over time.

size.description: The numbers' height, as a share of the frame's.

warn_color.description: The colour in the last seconds before zero.

TimerSettings.description: What a timer counts and how it writes it.

clock_24h.description: The time of day as 14:05, or as 2:05 PM.

clock_seconds.description: Seconds on the time of day.

duration_secs.description: How long a count down is, in seconds.

target_secs.description: The time of day counted to, in seconds after midnight.

warn_secs.description: Seconds before zero it turns the warning colour; never at 0.

TransportSource.description: Where the transport's position comes from.

TransportSyncMode.description:
Whether a video deck maps its playhead onto the show transport.

See /spec/timecode.md § Consumer 2.

oneOf.description: Apply a router path at a fixed value (e.g. `deck/<uuid>/trigger` → 1.0).

Param.description: Apply a router path at a fixed value (e.g. `deck/<uuid>/trigger` → 1.0).

oneOf.description: A global app action (undo/redo/save/tap-tempo).

TriggerAction.description: A discrete action fired by a Trigger button on its rising edge.

triggers.description: Discrete actions fired on a Trigger button's rising edge.

at.description: Omit to leave the position alone.

name.description: Omit to leave the name alone.

curve.description: Response curve applied before mapping into `[min, max]`.

invert.description: Flip the response (equivalent to swapping min/max).

max.description: Upper bound of the target's normalized sub-range (0.0–1.0). `min > max` inverts.

min.description: Lower bound of the target's normalized sub-range (0.0–1.0).

vertices.description: Vertex positions as [x, y] pairs in normalised coordinates.

VideoCodec.description: The video codec a stream or recording is encoded in.

position_secs.description: Seek position in seconds from the start of the video.
